printing.agentsHint: A small program installed on one computer in the restaurant (the register, a mini PC) that sends the POS's jobs to the printers. One per location is enough.
printing.deleteAgentConfirm: Delete this agent? Nothing will print until you install a new one.
printing.tokenOnce: Copy it now: for safety it is never shown again. If you lose it, delete the agent and create another.
printing.step3: Come back here, add your printers and pick this agent on each one.
printing.step1_windows: On the Windows PC next to the printers, download the file:
printing.step1_mac: On the Mac next to the printers, download the matching file:
printing.step1_linux: On the Linux computer next to the printers, download the file:
printing.step1_pi: On the Raspberry Pi, download the file matching its OS:
printing.step2_windows: Open PowerShell in the Downloads folder (right-click the folder → Open in Terminal) and run:
printing.step2_mac: Open Terminal, go to Downloads (cd Downloads) and run:
printing.step2_linux: Open a terminal in the downloads folder and run:
printing.step2_pi: Open a terminal in the downloads folder and run:
printing.warning_windows: The first time, Windows shows “Windows protected your PC” (SmartScreen). Click “More info”, then “Run anyway”. It appears because the program is not yet digitally signed with Microsoft, not because it is unsafe.
printing.warning_mac: macOS blocks programs not notarized by Apple; the xattr command clears that quarantine flag. If the warning still shows, go to Settings → Privacy & Security and click “Open Anyway”.
printing.warning_linux: If the system asks, allow it to run. Nothing else to install: the program has no dependencies.
printing.warning_pi: If the system asks, allow it to run. Nothing else to install: the program has no dependencies.
printing.step3_windows: To start with the PC: Task Scheduler → Create Basic Task → “When I log on” → “Start a program” pointing at the .exe (the token is no longer needed).
printing.step3_mac: To start with the Mac: Settings → General → Login Items → “+” and pick the file (the token is no longer needed).
printing.step3_linux: To start with the machine, create a systemd service (template in the agent's README).
printing.step3_pi: To start with the Pi, create a systemd service (template in the agent's README).
printing.printersHint: Each printer connects over the network (cable or Wi-Fi, port 9100) or by USB to the agent's computer.
printing.kindNetworkHint: The printer's IP on your network. Pin it in the router so it never changes.
printing.kindSystemHint: The printer installed on the agent's computer, with the exact name Windows or the system shows.
printing.agentNeeded: Add an agent first; without one nothing reaches the printer.
printing.stationsHint: With none picked it takes every station's tickets. With one or more, only those.

flows.modeAiDesc: The AI asks its own way and captures the flow's data.
flows.modeLinearDesc: The bot follows the flow exactly as drawn.

flows.dropoffHint: Which question customers were on when they didn't finish.

flows.confirmHint: Sent with Yes / No buttons. Use captured answers as variables.
flows.fieldEndBodyHint: Optional. Sent when the flow ends.
flows.actionHint: What the bot does when it passes this node.
flows.fieldSlotLabelHint: How it shows in the inbox and how the AI understands it.
flows.fieldSlotKeyHint: Identifier for variables and conditions (no spaces).

tutorial.title: Tutorials
tutorial.subtitle: Learn the POS and the host stand step by step, with a demo you can tap.
tutorial.demoNote: The demo starts in explain mode: tap any button and it tells you what it does. Turn it off at the top to try it for real; nothing is saved.
tutorial.pos_intro: Charge at the counter or at the table, send to the kitchen, close the register.
tutorial.pos_open_b: Under “Register” tap “Open register” and enter your starting cash. Nothing can be charged while it is closed.
tutorial.pos_sell_b: Tap products on the grid; the first one starts a quick sale. Use the category chips, the search (⌘K) or a barcode scanner.
tutorial.pos_options_b: Products marked “+” open their options sheet (size, extras, no onion…). The pencil on a line edits it later.
tutorial.pos_table_b: In the current sale tap “Table” to set or change it, “Customer” to name it and “Guests” to split the bill.
tutorial.pos_charge_b: “Checkout” opens payment: tip, method (cash, card, transfer), tendered amount and change. Partial payments are fine.
tutorial.pos_customer_b: From the sidebar open the customer screen on the second display: it shows the order, the total, then the change and a thank-you.
tutorial.pos_kitchen_b: “Send to kitchen” fires the new lines to the KDS by station. Sent lines show ✓ kitchen.
tutorial.pos_close_b: At the end of the shift, “Close register”: count the cash (total or by denomination) and Kuik prints the Z report with sales by method and the difference.
tutorial.host_intro: The live floor plan, waitlist and the day’s bookings, for the tablet at the door.
tutorial.host_plan_b: Tap “Edit floor”: add tables with a name, seats and shape, drag them into place and group them by room. Join tables under “Combinations” for large parties.
tutorial.host_lists_b: Waitlist, Reservations (by scheduled time) and Seated (by seated time). Each row: party size, time or timer, name with tags, and the table on the right.
tutorial.host_book_b: “Book” takes a future reservation. In the Waitlist, the chips show the estimated wait per party size; tap one or the “+” to add someone without a booking.
tutorial.host_arrive_b: Tap the reservation and choose “Arrived” or “Partially arrived”. A booking past the grace period turns yellow as “Late”.
tutorial.host_seat_b: “Seat” or the crosshair button: the plan suggests free tables that fit (and combinations). Tap one or more tables and confirm. The table takes its colour and the timer starts.
tutorial.host_status_b: Tap a busy table to move its status: seated, appetizer, entrée, dessert, check, paid, bussing. Each has its own colour on the plan. Past the turn time a red ring appears.
tutorial.host_waitlist_b: On a waiting party tap “Table ready” to send the WhatsApp; it becomes “Notified” and the timer turns yellow or red past the quoted wait.
tutorial.host_finish_b: “Finish” frees the table and moves the visit to Finished. In settings (gear) you define shifts, turn times by party size and the grace minutes.
tutorial.openTab: Open tutorial in a new tab
tutorial.kds_intro: Where tickets land per station, with a timer and urgency colours.
tutorial.kds_arrive_b: When the POS “sends to kitchen”, a ticket per station appears here with a chime. Oldest on the left.
tutorial.kds_read_b: Big quantity, dish, modifiers in blue and notes in yellow. The header changes colour with age: blue, amber at 5 minutes, red at 10.
tutorial.kds_start_b: Tap “Start” when you begin. Strike items off one by one by tapping them.
tutorial.kds_ready_b: “Ready” turns it green for the pass. “Served” clears it; if that was a mistake, “Recall” below brings it back for 15 minutes.
tutorial.kds_station_b: With the station chips, or by opening /kds?station=Bar, each screen sees only its own. Stations are set per menu category.
tutorial.kds_allday_b: “All day” adds up how many of each dish are still to make across all tickets.

help.hint: Tap any button or area to learn what it does
help.generic_b: No description yet. Turn explain mode off to use it.
help.pos_nav_sale_b: The main screen: products on the left, the current sale on the right. This is where you charge.
help.pos_nav_tables_b: Floor map. Tap a free table to open a tab on it or a busy one to pick up its sale. Uses the host stand's plan if there is one.
help.pos_nav_orders_b: Every open or held tab with its total and server. The badge is how many there are.
help.pos_nav_history_b: Sales charged this shift. Reprint a ticket or reopen a tab from here.
help.pos_nav_register_b: Open and close the shift's register, and open the customer screen.
help.pos_customerScreen_b: Opens what the customer sees on the second display: their order, the total and, on payment, the change.
help.pos_kitchen_b: Opens the kitchen screen, where orders sent with “Send to kitchen” arrive.
help.pos_settings_b: Goes to the Orders settings: number of tables, cash count and payment methods.
help.pos_server_b: The server or cashier on this device. Every sale is tagged with them.
help.pos_search_b: Type a name or code, or fire the barcode scanner. A single match is added with Enter. Shortcut ⌘K.
help.pos_hold_b: Parks the current sale without charging and clears the screen. Pick it up again under Tabs.
help.pos_newSale_b: Starts an empty sale. The previous one stays open under Tabs.
help.pos_registerChip_b: Green: register open, you can charge. Amber: closed. Tap to go to Register.
help.pos_bell_b: Whether the POS is online and how many operations are still to upload. It works offline and syncs when back.
help.pos_fullscreen_b: Hides the browser so the POS fills the tablet.
help.pos_tableCard_b: Coloured: it has an open tab and shows its total. Plain: free; tapping opens a tab tied to that table.
help.pos_tabCard_b: Tap to load it in Sales. “Held” are sales parked with the Hold button.
help.pos_registerButton_b: Opening asks for the starting cash. Closing counts the cash and Kuik builds the shift report.
help.pos_openCustomer_b: On a two-screen device it opens on the second one. With one screen it opens in a window you can move.
help.pos_newTab_b: Opens a tab with a name or table up front, before adding products.
help.pos_category_b: Filters products by menu section. “All” shows everything.
help.pos_popular_b: The products sold most on this device, one tap away.
help.pos_product_b: One tap adds it to the sale. With a “+” it first opens its options (size, extras, no onion…).
help.pos_saleMenu_b: Discount, customer, table, guests, hold or void the tab.
help.pos_switchTab_b: The other open tabs. Tap to switch between them without losing anything.
help.pos_line_b: A product on the tab with its options. “✓ kitchen” means it was already sent.
help.pos_qty_b: Add or remove units. The pencil reopens the options to change them.
help.pos_remove_b: Deletes the line from the sale. Not possible once paid.
help.pos_totals_b: Subtotal, discount and tip if any, and the total to charge.
help.pos_fire_b: Sends the new lines to the kitchen screen, split by station. The number is how many are still unsent.
help.pos_checkout_b: Opens payment with the total: tip, method, tendered amount and change. Needs an open register.
help.pos_payMethod_b: Opens checkout with that method already picked: cash, card, transfer or other.
help.pos_scan_b: Focuses the search so a barcode scanner adds products directly.
help.pos_discount_b: An amount or percentage on the tab, with 10, 15, 20, 50 % and comp shortcuts.
help.pos_customer_b: Name the tab so you recognise it (takeaway, bar, etc.).
help.pos_table_b: Assign or change this tab's table. With a plan you pick from the grid; without one you type it.
help.pos_guests_b: How many people at the table. Used to split the bill.
help.pos_void_b: Cancels the whole tab with a reason. It stays on record as voided.
help.pos_cartBar_b: On small screens the sale lives here: items and total; tap to open it in full.
help.host_view_floor_b: The table map with live status. The host's main view.
help.host_view_timeline_b: One row per table across the shift's hours. Each party is a bar as long as its turn time; the green line is now.
help.host_view_list_b: Every list in full, including Finished and Cancelled / no-shows.
help.host_search_b: Find someone by name or phone across the day's lists.
help.host_covers_b: People seated right now / total expected today.
help.host_date_b: Switch days to view or prepare another date. “Today” returns to the current date.
help.host_shift_b: The shift in progress (Lunch, Dinner…). Set in Settings.
help.host_pending_b: Requests on other days nobody has accepted. Tap to see them in the dashboard.
help.host_book_b: Take a reservation for today or another day: name, phone, party, time and area.
help.host_settings_b: Shifts, turn time by party size and grace minutes before a booking shows as “Late”.
help.host_seatingBar_b: Tap one or more tables on the plan and confirm. Suggested are free tables that fit the party, combinations included.
help.host_rooms_b: Switch between rooms: dining room, patio… Each has its own plan.
help.host_editPlan_b: Drag tables to move them, double-tap to add, tap one to change name, seats or shape. Combinations are created here too.
help.host_section_waitlist_b: Walk-ins waiting for a table. Shows parties and covers; the arrow collapses it.
help.host_section_reservations_b: Today's bookings by time, not yet seated. Yellow = late, green = arrived.
help.host_section_seated_b: Parties at a table, by seated time, with how long they have been there and their turn time. Red = over.
help.host_section_finished_b: Visits that have left. They can be reopened.
help.host_section_removed_b: Bookings cancelled or marked as no-show.
help.host_addWalkIn_b: Someone without a booking: party, name, phone and quoted wait, or seat them right away.
help.host_quote_b: How long a party of that size would wait, from free tables and turn times. Tap to add a walk-in with that quote.
help.host_row_b: The colour stripe is its status. Tap for details and actions: confirm, arrived, seat, no-show, notify…
help.host_tableBadge_b: The party's table. Coloured, it shows where in the meal they are (appetizer, entrée, dessert, check…).
help.host_assign_b: Enters seating mode: pick the table on the plan and the party moves to Seated.
help.host_table_b: Each table tells its story with its colour and what is written on it. Grey: free, the small number is its seats. Lavender with a time (e.g. 14:21): a booking arrives at that time, so do not fill it with something long; the circle is the party size. Coloured with an icon: the party is seated and the icon says where they are (appetizer, entrée, dessert, check, paid, bussing). Red dot or border: they are past their turn time. Below, the server working it. Tap the table to see the party or seat someone.
help.host_addTable_b: Creates a new table on the plan: name, seats, shape and room.
help.kds_filters_b: Show every ticket or only new, cooking or ready ones. The number is how many there are.
help.kds_stations_b: Each station (kitchen, bar, grill…) sees only its own. Set per menu category. ?station= in the URL pins a screen to one.
help.kds_stats_b: Average minutes open tickets have been waiting, and the oldest. The oldest turns red past 10 minutes.
help.kds_allDay_b: Opens the panel that adds up how many of each dish are still to make across all tickets, for batch cooking.
help.kds_mute_b: Mute or unmute the chime: it sounds one way for a new ticket and another when one passes 10 minutes.
help.kds_theme_b: Dark for dim kitchens, light for screens in sunlight.
help.kds_fullscreen_b: Hides the browser so the kitchen screen fills the monitor.
help.kds_ticket_b: One ticket per station and per send from the POS. Oldest first, on the left.
help.kds_ticketHead_b: Table or counter, station and status. Colour is age: blue new, amber past 5 minutes, red past 10 (pulses), green ready for pickup.
help.kds_timer_b: Minutes and seconds since it was sent to the kitchen.
help.kds_lines_b: Big quantity, name, modifiers in blue and notes in yellow. Tap an item to strike it off as it is done; handy on large tickets.
help.kds_bump_b: Start → Ready → Served. “Ready” tells the pass it can be picked up; “Served” clears the ticket from the screen.
help.kds_print_b: Prints the ticket on the kitchen printer, for teams that prefer paper.
help.kds_allDayPanel_b: Sum of every pending dish across new and cooking tickets. Recalculates on its own.
help.kds_recall_b: The last served tickets, for 15 minutes. Tap one bumped by mistake and it comes back as ready.
